title: Simple maths and strings
summary: Use math operators and join text.

steps.note: The plus sign adds numbers together. Python calculates the result.

choices.why: Correct. Python adds the two numbers and prints 5.
Quotes make one piece of text, so Python will not do the addition.
The minus sign subtracts. Use plus to add these numbers.

steps.explain: The + operator adds 2 and 3, giving the number 5.

steps.note: The minus sign subtracts the number on the right from the number on the left.

choices.why: Correct. Eight minus three is five.
That adds the numbers. This step is about subtraction.
Quotes turn the expression into text instead of a calculation.

steps.note: In Python, an asterisk means multiply.

choices.why: Correct. The asterisk multiplies four by three.
Python uses * for multiplication, not the letter x.
The plus sign adds; it does not multiply.

steps.explain: The * operator multiplies the two numbers to get 12.

steps.note: The plus sign can join text too. Add a space string between words when you need a space.

choices.why: Correct. The three text pieces join into Hello world.
This joins the words with no space between them.
Python cannot subtract text. Use + to join strings.

steps.explain: Each quoted piece is text, and + joins the pieces together.

steps.note: Quoted digits are text. Adding two text values joins them instead of doing arithmetic.

choices.why: Correct. Both values are text, so the result is 55.
These are numbers, so Python adds them to get 10.
Python cannot multiply one text value by another text value.

steps.explain: Because both 5s are quoted, + joins the text to make 55.

steps.note: Without quotes, 5 and 5 are numbers. Adding them gives ten, not the text 55.

choices.why: Correct. These are numbers, so Python calculates their sum.
Quotes make these text, which joins into 55.
The asterisk multiplies; this step asks you to add.

steps.explain: Unquoted digits are numbers, so 5 + 5 evaluates to 10.
